chapter_meta_description: Yuchi Xiyue secures Golden Armored Imperial Guards for Ji Ning. King Yan tests Ji Ning's Dao-heart with his terrifying killing intent. A family bond is forged in the Grand Xia capital.
og_title: King Yan's Judgment: Ji Ning Passes the Dao-Heart Trial
og_description: A Celestial Immortal's killing intent meets an unmovable sword-soul. Yuchi Xiyue fights for her brother's safety in the Grand Xia capital.
twitter_title: Xiyue's fierce protection and Yan Wang's terrifying grace
twitter_description: Family politics, Golden Armored Imperial Guards, and a Dao-heart test that Ji Ning aces—this chapter is Xianxia power chess at its finest.

lore_anchors.definition: The nickname of King Yan, a Celestial Immortal known for his overwhelming killing intent; also the Chinese name for Yama, King of Hell.
Elite guards of the Grand Xia royal clan, typically assigned only to royalty but can be gifted to others as a personal favor.
The ultimate refined essence of natural energy, used as a high-value currency among cultivators; one million catties is an enormous sum.
A portable magical residence that can be carried by a cultivator; requires at least the Wanxiang stage to refine and carry.
The mountain peak inside the Yan Estate that King Yan favors for solitary contemplation and Dao meditation.
A Loose Immortal or Earth Immortal-level servant-assassin of the Shaoyin clan, tasked with killing Ji Ning.
An ancient and powerful clan that has a vendetta against Yuchi Xiyue and Ji Ning; Patriarch Xuanji is a feared and unreasonable Celestial Immortal.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does King Yan want to test Ji Ning’s Dao-heart?
cultural_notes_faq.a: King Yan is a Celestial Immortal who ascended through slaughter—his killing intent is so intense it can break weaker cultivators’ wills. He wants to see if Ji Ning is strong enough to deserve his granddaughter’s trust and his own protection. Passing this test is a massive endorsement.

cultural_notes_faq.q: How can Yuchi Xiyue give Ji Ning an Imperial Guard squad?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The Golden Armored Imperial Guards were gifted to King Yan personally by the Emperor. While *custom* says they usually guard royalty, no *law* prohibits King Yan from assigning them to a trusted guest. Xiyue exploits this loophole with a mix of strategic argument and affectionate blackmail.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What makes Ji Ning’s portable immortal mansion so special?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It’s an extremely rare and valuable item—worth a million catties of Primordial Liquid—that can only be refined at the Wanxiang level. It’s not just a luxury residence; it also serves as a hidden vault for the aquatic palace (the Water Mansion/his secret treasure inheritance), making it a critical asset for his safety.
